thread:
sarah_lin: quick thought — we should add a visible audit + testing sandbox for automatic fallback rules in the Rollouts page. currently it's too hidden and people are nervous about silent model switches.

mike_p: +1. what do you mean by 'audit'? like a change log or decision trace for each request? :thinking:

sarah_lin: both. i want two things: (1) an easy preview that shows what would have happened for the last N minutes if the auto-fallback had been enabled, and (2) a per-request decision trace (reason code, metric snapshot, model chosen, cached hit) we can view in the console.

alex_g: agree. ops teams will want an immutable record for compliance. also we should include sampling controls — full traces are huge. default to 1% with an opt-in for 100% for flagged routes.

juli: happy path UX: on the Rollouts config, add a small panel "Auto-degrade policy" with: threshold sliders, degraded mode chooser (soft/hard/cache/circuit-breaker), and a preview toggle. clicking preview runs a background sim against recent telemetry and shows "X% requests would have degraded".

mike_p: can we sketch the policy DSL? something tiny that teams can understand and copy/paste. e.g.:
```
when error_rate > 5% for 2m then fallback to model:fast-gpt-small mode:hard cooldown:5m reason:ERROR_SPIKE
when latency_p95 > 1200ms then mode:soft adjust:temperature=0.2 reason:HIGH_LATENCY
```

alex_g: nice. add a `require_approval: true|false` flag so enterprise customers can force manual approval for any automatic fallback.

sarah_lin: console should surface audit entries like:
- timestamp
- request_id (sampled)
- route
- original_model, chosen_model
- reason_code
- metric_snapshot (p95, error_rate)
- policy_version
- rollout_id

ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: route=/api/v1/chat spikes in 5xx -> 7.2% over 3m (detected by metrics-agent)

juli: on the UI, we could show a small "What happened" timeline: e.g., 11:12 policy triggered (reason=ERROR_SPIKE), 11:13 fallback enacted -> model switched to x, 11:18 policy cooled down. link to trace.

mike_p: regarding telemetry, need these fields in the per-route dashboard: error_rate, retcode distribution (4xx/5xx), p50/p95 latency, model_queue_depth, cache_hit_rate, tokens_per_request. add a column for "policy_effect" (delta in latency/cost/quality).

alex_g: quality is harder — maybe tie to evaluation hooks: have a small set of golden prompts (per-route) that run in background to estimate drift when fallback occurs. show regression alert if quality drops > threshold.

sarah_lin: +1. also we must expose the exact decision reason codes as enums so customers can wire alerts to PagerDuty. example codes: ERROR_SPIKE, LATENCY_SPIKE, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, MANUAL_ROLLBACK, HEALTHCHECK_FAIL

juli: ops question — what about cache-only fallback? serve from prefix cache instead of switching models. UX should show cache staleness and TTLs.

mike_p: implementation note: policy evaluation should happen in the control plane, but decision traces must be stamped on requests served by the runtime so they’re searchable in logs. we need a small proto field `fallback_reason` and `policy_version` added to request headers for telemetry.

alex_g: and a compact audit log format for retention: JSONL entries with reason + bake-in policy id. default retention 90d; enterprise can extend.

sarah_lin: final ask: put a guardrail in the Rollouts UI — a calculated risk score and an "Enable automatic fallback" checkbox with an inline explanation and a quick simulated impact (latency/cost/estimated quality). default to OFF for new policies.

mike_p: can someone take a quick mock for the panel? @juli want you to own the mock. i'll draft the small DSL + proto changes and open a PR.

juli: will do a mock by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

sarah_lin: thanks — i'll write the acceptance criteria for the sim and auditing requirements.

ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: rollout ui changes scheduled to staging at 2026-03-20T02:00Z (automated message)

mike_p: leaving a note — we should also add an "explain mode" button that replays decision logic for a single request step-by-step. helpful for root-cause during incidents.

alex_g: +1. and an API endpoint to fetch the decision trace by request_id so external SRE tools can integrate.

sarah_lin: perfect. i'll create the RFC doc and link it in this thread once it's up. thanks all!
